# Software Requirements Specification (SRS)

<!-- Generated by `omni docs build` (REQ-060) for Arbiter. Do not edit; regenerate. -->

What Arbiter must do. One row per requirement in `.ai/requirements/requirements.json`, grouped by area: its status, priority, how many tests are linked to it, and the first sentence of its description. Acceptance criteria follow for the requirements that are still open.

Which tests and files belong to each requirement is in the [Requirements Traceability Matrix](requirements-traceability.md); the validation each one asks for is in the [Test Plan and Coverage Summary](test-plan.md). For a single requirement in full run `omni requirement show <id>`; `omni docs build --detail full` writes every requirement in full here. Change requirements with `omni requirement add|update|complete`, never here.

## Acceptance criteria of open requirements

Completed and withdrawn requirements are left out; their criteria are in the registry.

### ARB-005: Establish licensing terms for arbiter

1. a LICENSE file exists at the repository root and pyproject.toml references it
2. copyright ownership is asserted
3. ownership of scan output is assigned to the user
4. the redistribution review for bundled analyzers is recorded in NOTICE.md with a date and a reviewer

### ARB-055: Flag worker loops with no stop signal and non-daemon threads

1. fires on a planted fixture
2. silent when a stop event or context cancellation is checked

### ARB-056: Flag swallowed errors in worker loops with no retry or dead-letter path

1. worker-loop context raises severity
2. silent when the error is logged and re-queued

### ARB-057: Flag outbound HTTP and DB calls without a timeout in TypeScript, Java and Go

1. fires on planted fetch/HttpClient/http.Get fixtures
2. silent when a timeout or context deadline is set

### ARB-058: Tests call sys.executable instead of a bare python

1. suite passes on a machine with only python3

### ARB-062: CWE Top 25 coverage per IDE language, with what is not assessed stated

1. per-language CWE table in docs/probes.md (not assessed / gap) and the matrix in docs/cwe-top25.md
2. each applicable cell has a planted pair under fixtures/planted/<lang>/; a caught defect carries expect: or expect-ext:, an uncaught one carries gap: CWE-N
3. planted_score.py stays fully caught with 0 on good twins and 0 unmarked, native-only and with --adapters
4. the ranked gaps from docs/cwe-top25.md get native rules, each turning its gap: comment into an expect: marker
5. not-assessed CWEs appear in the controls coverage output: needs a CWE Top 25 control pack with per-language applicability (a control today has one automatable value and no language), a state or reason for 'does not apply in this language' distinct from not_automatable, and controls._probe_of mapping arbiter/<lang>.* to the lang_<lang> probe (today it returns '<lang>', so a language-pack check would always read as not assessed)

### ARB-063: Install and test on Windows, Linux and macOS

1. pr-check matrix includes macos-latest and windows-latest with analyzers
2. planted corpus passes on all three
3. CI-shape tests require macos

### ARB-064: Every finding traceable in OmniGraph: rule, CWE, file, requirement, commit

1. omni graph why <finding> shows file symbol rule cwe requirement and introducing commit
2. omni graph impact <file> lists findings
3. works in interview-ide-arbiter after make scan

### ARB-066: Remediation through MCP, with a verify loop

1. arbiter explain/fix <finding> returns a patch-shaped suggestion and a verify command for every native rule
2. MCP tool returns the same structure; a schema test pins it
3. applying the planted good twin's change to its bad file makes the finding disappear for every planted defect
4. verify reports pass/fail per step (probe, tests, gate)

### ARB-067: Explain why a rule fired or did not fire; feed verdicts back into confidence

1. why and why-not work for every native pack rule
2. a recorded false-positive verdict lowers that rule's reported confidence on the next scan, with the verdict cited
3. precision per rule over the clean and gold corpora is published in docs/
4. gaps and next-steps report written (docs/gaps-and-next-steps.md)

### ARB-068: Auto-apply fixes only for rules whose fixes verify reliably

1. per-rule fix verification rate is measured and stored
2. only rules at or above the threshold are eligible
3. each applied fix is its own commit citing the finding id and the verify result
4. security-dimension rules require an explicit reviewer approval

### ARB-069: Claims need evidence: agent and PR claims carry the command that proves them

1. a claims block format is documented and parsed
2. omni gate reruns each claim's command and compares the result
3. a mismatched claim fails the gate with the expected and actual values

### ARB-070: Assumption ledger linked in OmniGraph

1. assumptions are stored in the registry or a sibling file with a schema
2. omni graph shows requirement-to-assumption-to-evidence edges
3. completing a requirement with an unverified assumption fails the registry gate

### ARB-071: Briefs and instructions generated from code, or tested against it

1. agent brief sections listing schema and commands are generated
2. every hand-written engine capability claim in packs/ and docs/ has a test
3. the #not-match? claim is covered by a test

### ARB-072: Environment preflight before every agent or scan run

1. arbiter preflight prints and stores import path, branch, HEAD, tool versions and pack compile status
2. a mismatch between the expected and actual import path fails
3. reports include the preflight record

### ARB-073: Independent mechanical re-verification of agent reports

1. a re-verify command takes a branch and a report and reruns every claimed check
2. discrepancies are reported per claim
3. merging an agent branch is blocked until re-verification passes

### ARB-074: Label statements as verified, inferred or assumed; flag lossy input

1. report and brief schemas carry a per-claim label
2. inputs passed through compression or truncation are marked in the record
3. a conclusion drawn only from lossy input is labelled inferred

### ARB-075: Ask instead of guessing on decisions the user owns

1. workflow instructions list the decision classes that require asking
2. skills record each question asked and the answer in the session log
3. a default chosen without asking is stated in the output

### ARB-097: Build a Python SQL injection oracle-conformance pilot

1. Select a licensed independently labelled Python CWE-89 dataset or explicitly stop on unresolved clearance
2. Keep machine-oracle evaluation data separate from development and regression pairs
3. Define aggregate-only evaluation outputs that do not expose sealed per-example data
4. Record pinned source evaluator and runtime metadata
5. Report precision recall denominators and uncertainty without generalizing beyond the benchmark
6. Keep existing detection rules unchanged until source and protocol are approved

### ARB-101: Held-out set r5: 50 repositories frozen before scanning, 1,010 model labels

1. repo list committed before scan
2. every sampled finding labelled
3. labels recorded with source heldout-r5-model

### ARB-110: Close recall gap without human reviewers: development-only recall analysis and preregistered model-labelled sample

1. Recall-gap table from development data only with denominators
2. Preregistration frozen before any evaluation labels are produced
3. Training/evaluation split by repository with no sealed or evaluation leakage
4. Results labelled model-labelled conformance
5. No 99 percent claim

### ARB-153: Turn on adaptive quality thresholds and pin them per repository

1. arbiter profile writes a per-repository profile and moves the knowledge version
2. a scan with a learned profile reports profile_source learned and one without reports measured
3. profiles are keyed so two repositories never share an entry
4. a profile under 30 samples leaves the fixed threshold in place
5. the configured threshold caps the adaptive one; so a uniformly bad codebase cannot raise its own limit and a tenfold uniform degradation cannot leave the flagged set unchanged

### ARB-162: Held-out set r7 (Python): 20 pinned repositories frozen before scanning

1. the list was committed before any repository was cloned
2. every repository is pinned to a commit SHA
3. every skipped candidate is recorded with a reason

### ARB-163: Breadth set r7 Python: 180 applications frozen, dev/held-out split, scanned on pods

1. manifest committed before any clone
2. no repo used before
3. no Windows-invalid paths
4. pod spend reported

### ARB-169: Workstream D: twelve statistical methods for precision, labelling cost and catch rate

_None recorded._

### ARB-172: Capture-recapture catch-rate estimate across Arbiter, Semgrep and Bandit (D6)

1. Matching rule documented and unit-tested
2. Only tp-labelled or ground-truth findings enter capture histories
3. Simulated independent detectors give nominal CI coverage and correlated detectors a documented downward bias
4. Benchmark validation reports estimate vs true total
5. Development results per language and family with intervals
6. Deterministic output
7. Labelling spend at most 20 USD with plan committed before any call

### ARB-176: Precision reportable per language, JavaScript apart from TypeScript

1. a .js finding of the TypeScript pack is a javascript stratum
2. a split stratum's population is not counted twice
3. report prints one claim per language
4. ledger and packaged copy byte-identical
5. backfill --check passes
